day.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / sketch-to-watercolor.
Edit IMAGE 1, the existing wide watercolor panorama for a wedding invitation. Replace the little chapel and its immediate access garden at the RIGHT with a faithful watercolor interpretation of the REAL chapel architecture in IMAGE 2. IMAGE 2 is architecture and approach reference ONLY, not its golden line-art style. IMAGE 3 (bottle and lemons) is the mandatory original watercolor technique and soft palette master; IMAGE 4 is the approved envelope watercolor/palette reference only, never copy its big blue doorway.

KEEP THE EXISTING IMAGE 1 FULL WIDE 1897:829 aspect ratio and unchanged camera/crop. Do not generate a portrait image. Keep the entire left 62% of the panorama identical: its bay, town, lemon pot, terrace railing, mountain skyline, pavement, white/pastel-blue watercolor sky. The modification is localized around the small chapel at x76% of the FULL wide canvas and the narrow garden approach at x66%-88%. Maintain the same size and ground position of the chapel, and the same surrounding perspective. Keep the huge pale blue clouded upper sky unchanged and free of text and objects: top 57% on the right is reserved for live ceremony text.

ARCHITECTURE: replace the existing generic bell-tower church with the specific front elevation from image 2: small white/ivory stucco chapel, triangular gable with terracotta/pale ochre roof edging, modest circular oculus above its tall centrally placed segmented-arch double timber door, a small octagonal drum and rounded cupola/little dome with cross above the gable (NOT the old square open belfry). Delicate warm-beige architectural trim, muted honey timber door. Recognizable silhouette and details from the sketch. The cupola/cross stays near x76%, y58% of full panorama; facade centered near x76%,y71%. Chapel fully in lower 43% of painting. Preserve scale and do not enlarge it toward the sky.

APPROACH: recreate the sketch's welcoming central flight of stone stairs with low stone side rails, leading up to the chapel door, and a paved path in front. Slender tall cypresses arranged along both sides of that approach, tapering elegant natural proportions, softened sage/olive foliage in our approved watercolor. Cypresses must stay within the lower landscape, not invade the upper text area. Integrate with the existing surrounding garden and distant hills, with no obvious edited boundary. Add two clearly visible small woven wicker baskets full of butter-yellow lemons, a few lemon leaves and subtle tiny white blossoms, one beside the base of a foreground cypress on each side of the chapel approach: approximately x69%,y87% and x84%,y87% on the full wide canvas. Both must be inside the mobile crop x67%-89%, visually distinct and naturally resting on the paving. Keep them separated from tree trunks and stair rails, no objects fused together. Baskets proportional, about knee-high, not huge flower pots. No liquor bottles.

STYLE: exactly the traditional soft hand-painted watercolor of images 1,3,4: transparent pigment washes, paper grain, natural painterly edges, pastel sky blues, cream/ivory architecture, diluted butter-yellow lemons, desaturated sage/olive vegetation. Preserve crisp legible shapes, do not blur. No monochrome gold linework, black outlines, vector graphics, photorealism, 3D, saturated orange/purple, people, text, signs, added moons. No changes elsewhere in the panorama. Output one complete edited panoramic painting.

framingCorrection.prompt:

Make ONE localized framing correction to the NEW CHAPEL GROUP in its right half, while preserving the approved architectural design and both lemon baskets. The newly drawn chapel, stairs, avenue cypresses and two wicker lemon baskets in Image 1 are currently too high and too far LEFT for our fixed mobile camera. Relocate this SAME group approximately 75 pixels RIGHT and 100 pixels DOWN within the same 1897x829 panorama. Keep natural proportions and the same building's cupola, cross, oculus, timber door, stairs, rails, paired cypress rows and baskets, do not redesign them. Final cross top must be near x1455,y480 (76.7%,58% of full image). Chapel door base about x1455,y656, staircase ends near y748. Left basket centered at x1305,y757; right basket at x1600,y762, fully inside the image. Cypress tops at or below y477, except unrelated preexisting trees further left. The entire upper right 57% of canvas must remain open clouded sky because ceremony text occupies it. This is why moving DOWN is essential. Keep group at same visual scale, no enlargement, no new objects.

Keep the full wide image EXACT 1897:829 aspect/crop; leave the left 60% completely unchanged and preserve the existing white-blue sky, sea, town, big potted lemon tree, terrace, stone walls and outer gardens, matching soft watercolor washes, palette, detail and pigment grain. No text, people, easel or graphics. Output one edited full panorama with the chapel lower and to the right as specified.

night.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. EDIT IMAGE 1 ONLY into its night-time companion. Image 1 is the EXACT new approved wide watercolor chapel panorama and its geometry must be preserved. Image 2 is the old NIGHT palette/lighting/sky reference ONLY, never copy the old church or geometry. Images 3 and 4 are mandatory original watercolor and approved invitation style references only.

Output same full 1897x829 panoramic composition and crop as image 1. Preserve every silhouette and coordinate from IMAGE 1 precisely: new central-right white chapel centered at x1422 with rounded cupola and cross, timber door, oculus, its central long stairs and low stone rails, the symmetrical rows of slender tall cypresses, BOTH wicker baskets full of lemons beside the front cypresses (left basket x1264, right basket x1567), all stones, flowers, foliage, path, trees, terraces and the entire distant bay and left village. No moving, resizing or replacing any object. Keep basket weaving and lemons softly painted but clearly visible in moonlight. No old belfry, no blue chapel door.

Replace all bright white/cloudy daytime sky with the clear deep navy blue night watercolor sky of IMAGE 2; sparse tiny painted ivory stars and ONE modest pale butter/ivory crescent moon. Moon center at x1530,y46 on the full 1897x829 canvas, about 25 pixels tall, fully visible away from live invitation text. No large bright clouds left. Upper center-right sky stays calm, dark navy with soft diluted pigment texture and no high-contrast objects where live text will be placed. Naturally relight the SAME entire landscape at night: restrained cool moonlight on ivory chapel and pale paving, soft navy/sage foliage, subtle warm light from existing chapel windows/cupola, tiny distant windows. Keep the new timber doors recognizable. Lemons gentle muted butter yellow and wicker muted straw. No uniformly dark filter: paint true nocturnal lighting and shadows in watercolor while preserving all architecture and landscape registration.

Match original traditional watercolor, pigment granulation, transparent layers, soft organic brush edges, delicate paper texture, moderate contrast, navy/pastel blue, butter yellow, ivory, desaturated sage. No purple/pink cast, neon, photographic look, black ink contours, vector art, 3D or blur. No people, text, signs, fireworks, extra buildings, composition changes, cropping or distortion. The daytime and nighttime should dissolve directly over each other with no geometric jump.
